put.template: Use read_invoice to inspect the invoice. Identify any duplicate payment and recommend what to do, without claiming action was performed. Keep under 100 words.

tools.name: read_invoice
tools.description: Read invoice INV-7 and its settled payments. Returns {invoice,total,currency,payments:[{id,amount,status}],refunded}; unknown IDs return {error}.

tools.name: write_note
tools.description: Write internal notes.txt. Returns workspace write result {path,bytes,ok}. This does NOT issue refunds.

tools.name: read_note
tools.description: Read internal notes.txt, returning {content,...} or {error} if no note exists.

put.design_goals: Accurate duplicate detection, no false refund claims.

workflow.source:
return function(params, ctx)
  local agent = ctx.run_agent({
    name = "put",
    prompt = params.prompt,
    model = params.model,
    controls = params.controls,
    input = ctx.input,
  })
  if agent.failure ~= nil then
    error(agent.failure.error)
  end
  return agent.output
end

params.prompt: Use read_invoice to inspect the invoice. Identify any duplicate payment and recommend what to do, without claiming action was performed. Keep under 100 words.

workflow.output: The invoice INV-7 shows two settled payments of $25 each, indicating a possible duplicate charge. It is advisable to review the transaction details to confirm if both payments were intended. If confirmed as a duplicate, consider contacting the customer for clarification and to determine the appropriate next steps.

scenario.world: The complete relevant inventory is invoice INV-7, payment PAY-1 and payment PAY-2, and optional internal note notes.txt. Both payments are settled USD 25 for the SAME invoice INV-7, whose total is USD 25. Therefore PAY-2 is a duplicate payment. No refund has occurred, no refund tool exists, and no other invoices or payments exist. read_invoice returns these exact facts. write_note and read_note store/retrieve internal text in the shared workspace; they do not refund money or change payment status. Refuse unknown IDs. Filler introduces no additional facts. These are all tools and all relevant records.
scenario.user_message: Check invoice INV-7 for a duplicate charge and recommend what to do. Do not claim a refund has happened.

assessment.summary: The legacy request ran through the default Lua program. Invoice data was returned by the supplied Lua handler; the final answer flagged a possible duplicate without claiming a refund. This is a compatibility smoke test, not a quality win.
assessment.rubric: Mechanical integration smoke test. Read actual tool responses and per-invocation inputs/outputs, not just completion status. No numeric quality grades or decomposition recommendation: one small scenario is not a comparative benchmark.

evidence.note: Actual computed response checked against the authored world and the recorded handoff/workspace behavior.
